verdict.root_cause: At 20:11:36 UTC platform-automation set cart's image reference to the 2.2.0-cart-hotfix.2 tag [tr_c1755292fd68]. Within a minute cart's endpoints stopped accepting connections and then vanished from service discovery: frontend logs a dial timeout to a concrete cart IP:port at ~20:12:18 and later name resolution returning zero addresses [tr_6cd2e801b1b2]. Cart itself emitted no error signal — error ratio stayed near baseline with 24 intervals of no span traffic at all, i.e. nothing was serving [tr_54634ff874e2]. The automation reverted the image at 20:20:51 [tr_c1755292fd68] and cart is logging normal cart-store operations by 20:38 [tr_30aff810f573]. The error bursts at frontend and frontend-proxy, with clean baselines and onset ~20:13, are bracketed by that update/revert pair [tr_0af772a00d1e][tr_67e6575efc29]. The running artifact on cart was briefly the wrong one and did not come up healthy; the caller-side errors are propagation [tr_bb55f0743c5a].
verdict.reasoning: Frontend's change log is empty [tr_bb55f0743c5a] and every retained frontend error stack ends at the gRPC client boundary carrying an upstream Unavailable from cart [tr_6cd2e801b1b2], so frontend and frontend-proxy are noticing, not causing. Cart is the named dependency and the only service with a change adjacent to onset. The mechanism is not application errors from cart — its error ratio never departs from baseline [tr_54634ff874e2] — but endpoints that refuse connections and then disappear from discovery [tr_6cd2e801b1b2], the signature of replicas replaced by an artifact that never became ready; the 24 no-traffic intervals corroborate [tr_54634ff874e2]. Timing is tight both ways: image set 20:11:36, first transport failures 20:12:18, metric change point ~20:13 [tr_0af772a00d1e][tr_67e6575efc29], revert 20:20:51, last retained frontend errors ~20:22, cart healthy by 20:38 [tr_30aff810f573]. The wrong artifact running is what broke the path, so bad_deploy and rollback — with the durable fix being to stop the automation loop that has applied and reverted this tag five times [tr_c1755292fd68].
open_questions: Cart's logs for 20:11-20:23 were truncated away [tr_30aff810f573], so the artifact's actual failure mode (crash on start, failed readiness, kill) is unobserved; the image-to-endpoint-loss link is inferred from timing and caller symptoms.
No pod availability, restart count, or CPU/memory data was fetched for cart [tr_54634ff874e2]; an OOM or crash-loop on the new image would look identical from the caller.

frontend-proxy shows a second threshold crossing ~20:35, after the revert and after frontend's retained errors stop [tr_67e6575efc29]; no per-route or per-upstream dimension was available to explain it, and one unmeasured edge was never crossed.

alternatives.root_cause: The hotfix image started but was killed for exceeding a memory or CPU limit, so cart replicas churned out of service discovery.
alternatives.why_not: No resource-limit or scaling change exists in cart's change log [tr_c1755292fd68] and no saturation or restart metric was retrieved [tr_54634ff874e2]; even if true it only refines how the wrong artifact died.

alternatives.root_cause: A service-discovery or network-layer disruption independent of the deploy cut frontend off from cart's endpoints.
alternatives.why_not: The earliest errors resolve a concrete cart IP and port before timing out, so discovery was intact at onset [tr_6cd2e801b1b2], and the outage begins and ends within minutes of the image set and revert [tr_c1755292fd68] — coincidence that tight is implausible.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change should be observed. The expected trajectory without intervention is the one already in evidence: cart's image was reverted by platform-automation at 20:20:51 [tr_c1755292fd68] and cart was logging normal ValkeyCartStore operations continuously through 20:39:02 [tr_30aff810f573]. Frontend and frontend-proxy error ratios should therefore decay to their flat-zero baselines on their own as retries drain, measurable on the same span-metrics error-ratio queries already used for both services.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is falsified if frontend or frontend-proxy error ratio is still above the 5% threshold 15 minutes from now, or if frontend logs resume the 'cart failure ... Unavailable / no addresses' path after 20:39. That would mean the revert did not actually restore cart and an active fix is needed — but the fix would belong on cart, which is not a legal target here, so the correct follow-up is to re-scope the blast radius to include cart rather than to act on frontend. A second, narrower falsifier: frontend-proxy's ~20:35 crossing [tr_67e6575efc29] recurring after cart is confirmed healthy would indicate a distinct, unexplained proxy-side fault that no evidence here characterises and no permitted action is known to address.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is leaving an unexplained second frontend-proxy threshold crossing at ~20:35 unaddressed; it postdates the revert and has no per-route or per-upstream dimension to explain it [tr_67e6575efc29], so if it is a real independent fault, waiting costs time. The risk of the alternative — acting anyway — is larger: the only legal targets are frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator, and the diagnosis places the fault on cart. rollback_image on frontend fails its precondition outright, because frontend's change history is empty for the whole queried period [tr_bb55f0743c5a], so there is no prior tag and no in-window change to revert to; that action would be a blind container recreate of a healthy service. restart_service on frontend or frontend-proxy is also unjustified: the evidence points at a change on a dependency, not at process state on the target, and it is irreversible, discards in-process cache, and would cause a fresh connection-reset burst in the exact signal we are trying to watch recover.
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal, since nothing is executed. For contrast, had an action been taken: load-generator and every external caller traverse frontend-proxy to frontend, so recreating either container would reset in-flight connections for all synthetic and real traffic in this world and would contaminate the frontend and frontend-proxy error-ratio series used to confirm recovery, making the post-revert decay unreadable.
proposal.notes: Two independent reasons to abstain, either sufficient. (1) Target legality: the mechanism is a bad image on cart [tr_c1755292fd68], and caller-side errors at frontend and frontend-proxy are propagation of cart's Unavailable/no-endpoints condition [tr_6cd2e801b1b2]. cart is not among the services this brief declares legal. No permitted action on a legal target addresses the mechanism. (2) The condition is already remediated: the offending image was reverted at 20:20:51 and cart is serving normally by 20:38 [tr_c1755292fd68][tr_30aff810f573]. Acting now would remediate a fault that no longer exists. Verdict confidence is only medium and three material gaps remain open — cart's 20:11-20:23 logs truncated, no pod/restart/CPU/memory data for cart [tr_54634ff874e2], and the unexplained ~20:35 proxy crossing — which independently argue against committing an irreversible action. Recommended non-action follow-up, outside what this system may do: fetch cart restart count and pod availability for 20:11-20:23, and a per-upstream error breakdown for frontend-proxy around 20:35; also investigate the automation loop that applied and reverted this same tag five times [tr_c1755292fd68], since the recurrence, not the single deploy, is the durable defect.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alert at the frontend-proxy edge with the load generator alerting simultaneously indicates user-facing impact, not a lone warning-latency blip. No open incident covers it, and the proxy-to-frontend edge is the natural first place to look.
